$schema_note: Spec for recreating 'Blockly Selenium' (in-app name: Block Bots) from scratch in a new repository. Everything needed is here: architecture, every block with its fields, the UI, the WebSocket protocol, server-mode security, deployment and acceptance tests. The block catalog was generated from the real code.

project.name: Blockly Selenium
project.summary: A kid-friendly, Scratch-style block editor (custom-built, NOT the Blockly library) for building Selenium browser tests and web-scraping robots. Kids snap colourful blocks together, press Run, and a real browser works through the blocks while each block lights up, plays a note, and gets a tick or a plain-English error.
project.audience: Children and beginners; every message is friendly, short and jargon-free.
project.origin: Rebuilt from an earlier Blockly + Playwright + Flask prototype; that code is not needed.

tech_stack.frontend: Plain HTML/CSS/JavaScript ES modules, no framework, no build step. Google Font 'Fredoka'. Web Audio API for all sounds.
tech_stack.backend: Python 3.12+, FastAPI, uvicorn[standard] (WebSockets), Selenium 4 (Selenium Manager for local drivers), openpyxl (Excel).
tech_stack.browser: Local: Chrome / Edge / Firefox (visible or headless). Server: headless Chromium + chromium-driver from Debian.

repository_layout.server.py: FastAPI app: serves the editor and playground, saved-tests API (local only), /ws/ping and /ws/run WebSockets, run limits.
repository_layout.runner.py: Run class (browser lifecycle, variables, output, live frames, address guard) + one function per block registered with @block('type').
repository_layout.static/js/blocks.js: Block catalog (CATEGORIES, LIST of block definitions, field helpers, newBlock, cloneBlock).
repository_layout.static/js/editor.js: Workspace: rendering, palette, drag & drop, snapping, variables, run highlights, undo, context menu, zoom.
repository_layout.static/js/app.js: Toolbar, run over WebSocket, robot mascot, diary, live browser window, variables box, save/load/export, examples, runner status.
repository_layout.static/examples/index.json + *.json: Built-in example tests shown by the Examples button.
repository_layout.static/playground/: Practice website (index.html, frame.html, robot.svg, prices.csv) served by the runner at /playground.

local.behaviour: Opens the editor at http://localhost:8000 in the default browser. Tests drive a real, visible browser window on this computer. Tests can be saved on disk (Save/Open), files are written to scraped/ or a chosen folder.

server.start: BLOCKBOTS_SERVER=1 python server.py --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000 (the Dockerfile does this)
server.behaviour: For hosting on a public website: headless Chromium, live browser-window frames, nothing written to disk, saved-tests API and /shots /scraped mounts disabled, address guard, run limits.

env.BLOCKBOTS_MAX_RUNS: max simultaneous runs (default 2); extra runs wait with a log message
env.BLOCKBOTS_ORIGINS: regex of allowed page Origins for the WebSockets (default: localhost/127.0.0.1 any port, https://(www.)becomeaiengg.com)

run_modes.hosted_editor: The editor detects 'hosted' mode when opened with ?runner=<url-or-path> (e.g. ?runner=/blockly-runner behind a reverse proxy) OR when /ws/ping replies server:true. Hosted mode hides Save/Open and 'keep browser open', always shows the live browser window, keeps tests in localStorage, and shows a '🔴 robot offline' chip only when the runner doesn't answer (pinged on load and every 30 s).

ui.look_and_feel: Bright, rounded, playful. Light lavender background (#F4F1FF), dotted-grid canvas, purple→blue→teal gradient top bar, chunky blocks with inset bottom shadow, bouncy pop/shake animations, prefers-reduced-motion respected.
ui.layout: Top bar (66px) + 4-column grid: category rail (84px) | palette with search (330px) | canvas (1fr) | side panel (300px). Below 1280px columns shrink; below 960px the side panel hides.
top_bar: ✨ New (fresh workspace with a Start block; undoable)
📂 Open / 💾 Save (local mode only; server-side tests/)
Speed slider 🐢 🐌 🐇 🐆 🚀 = pause between steps 1.5 / 0.8 / 0.4 / 0.15 / 0 s
'🔴 robot offline' chip (hosted only, when the runner is unreachable)
■ Stop (visible while running) and big green ▶ Run
palette: Category rail: coloured circle icon + name per category; click scrolls the palette; active category highlights while scrolling
Search box filters blocks by label/type/category
Each category section lists its blocks rendered exactly as they look on the canvas (inputs not editable in the palette)
Variables section starts with a dashed '📦 box': '➕ Make a variable' button and one draggable chip per variable (chip has × to delete; refused with a message if the variable is still used)

blocks_rendering.stack: Rounded rectangle, label text and inline fields in a wrapping row; puzzle tab at the bottom (CSS ::after) and notch at the top
blocks_rendering.hat: The Start block: rounded top, 🚀 icon, no top notch; only allowed at the top of a stack
blocks_rendering.c: C-shaped container (repeat, if…, for each, repeat until): head row, left arm, inner stack (min height), foot

fields.text: White pill input, auto-width (CSS field-sizing:content, JS fallback)
fields.select: Darker pill dropdown in the category's dark colour
fields.var: Dropdown of the workspace variables (📦 name) plus '➕ new variable…' (prompts for a name)
fields.file: White pill button '📁 choose a file' / '📄 filename'; accepts .csv .tsv .xlsx .xlsm .json .txt up to 3 MB; stored as {name, data(base64)}
fields.variable_pill: When a text/number field's whole value is '{name}', it renders as an orange pill '📦 name ×' instead of an input

blocks_rendering.loose_stacks: Stacks not starting with Start are faded and get a tooltip; only Start stacks run
blocks_rendering.unknown_block: Grey block 'unknown block "type"' so old files still load

canvas_interactions: Drag from palette creates a block; drag a block on the canvas takes it AND every block below it

Snapping: nearest attach point within 70px horizontally / 40px vertically (scaled by zoom): after any block, top of a C-mouth, or above the first block of a stack (hat-less stacks only). A glowing bar in the dragged block's colour shows the snap spot
Drop on the palette or the 🗑️ trash (bottom-right) deletes with a 'poof' particle effect
Drop on empty canvas creates a new stack
Right-click block: Duplicate (block + children, offset 30px) / Delete block (only that block; the rest closes the gap). Right-click canvas: Clean up / Undo
Zoom − ⦿ + (0.6–1.5) and 🧹 Clean up (stacks in a column) at the canvas bottom-right
Canvas locked (no drag/edit) while a test runs

Variable drag: drag a palette chip or an existing pill onto any white text/number box on the canvas (target box gets an orange outline); dropping replaces the box with the pill; dragging a pill elsewhere moves it; dropping a pill on nothing removes it; × on a pill clears the box
Variables auto-appear: any variable named in a var field or used as {name} in a field is added to the variables list
run_feedback: Current block: yellow outline + gentle pulse + bump, scrolled into view
Passed block: green outline + green ✓ badge (top-right), and a rising pentatonic note per passed step
Failed block: red outline, shake, red ✗ badge and a speech bubble to the right with the plain-English reason
All passed: fanfare + confetti + happy robot; failure: 'wah-wah' + sad robot

side_panel.robot: Inline-SVG robot 'Bolt' with blinking eyes, antenna colour and mouth by mood (idle, thinking=blue blinking, happy=green + hop, sad=red + shake) and a speech bubble
side_panel.live_browser_window: Mini Chrome window: title bar with red/yellow/green dots, address bar showing the robot's current URL (title as tooltip), ⤢ button / click to enlarge to a centred modal (✕ to shrink). Shows JPEG frames from the runner; placeholder text before the first run. Always visible when hosted; locally only when the browser is hidden. Yellow glow while running
side_panel.variables_box: '📦 Variables' list: every variable name with its live value ('not set yet' before), lists as 'list · N: a, b, c…', tables as 'table · N rows'; a row flashes when its value changes
side_panel.diary: '📒 Test diary' log with icons: 🏁 start, 💡 info, ✅ step text, 🤖 say messages, ❌ failures, 📸 screenshots (thumbnail, click to save), 🕸️ scraped-data cards (name, size, preview list/table/text, ⬇ CSV button), 💾 saved/downloaded files, 📦 'Download all (JSON)' of scraped data at the end, 🏆 result. 🧽 clears it

ui.sounds: All synthesised (no files): click, pick-up, hover/snap-target tick, snap, drop, trash whoosh, start arpeggio, step notes on a C-major pentatonic scale, win fanfare, fail wah-wah, oops. Mute state saved in localStorage
ui.persistence: Workspace autosaves to localStorage key 'blockbots.workspace' as {name, scripts, variables}. Speed, keep-open and mute are remembered. First visit loads the Playground Demo example
ui.dialogs: Open/Examples share one modal list; toast notifications slide up from the bottom

workspace_model.variable_reference: A field value '{name}' (whole value) is shown as a pill; '{name}' inside longer text is replaced too. Variable names are sanitized to [A-Za-z0-9_].

runner_semantics.execution: Scripts starting with 'start' run in order on a background thread, sharing one browser. For each block: check stop/time limit, emit step 'running', fill {variables} into string fields, call the block function, emit 'pass' with its sentence (or 'fail' with a friendly reason; parents of a failed child are marked 'fail' too), send a live frame, then pause for the speed delay. Browser always quits at the end unless 'keep browser open' (local Chrome/Edge use detach).
runner_semantics.auto_browser: Any block needing a browser opens Chrome automatically if no 'open browser' block ran (logs a message).
runner_semantics.element_finding: WebDriverWait (default 10 s; server mode caps any wait at 60 s) for presence/visibility/clickability depending on the block; the found element flashes a pink outline in the page for 450 ms. Missing element: "I couldn't find \"#x\" on the page (I waited 10s)."
runner_semantics.friendly_errors: Timeouts, click intercepted, not interactable, stale element, invalid selector and WebDriver errors are translated to short kid-friendly sentences.
runner_semantics.url_helper: Missing scheme: localhost/127.0.0.1/192.168./10. get http://, everything else https://.
runner_semantics.variables: run.vars dict. remember(name, value, card) stores and emits {event:'var'}; scrape and load-file blocks also emit a {event:'scraped'} diary card. as_text formats lists 'a, b, c', tables row-wise, whole floats without .0. Numbers can be read out of text ('$12.99' -> 12.99).
runner_semantics.outputs: output(filename, bytes|text, mime): server mode -> {event:'download'} with base64 data; local -> write to out_dir (default scraped/, change with 'save files in folder') and emit {event:'file', name, url (if in scraped/), path}. File names get a -HHMMSS stamp.
runner_semantics.excel: openpyxl; first row bold; number-looking text written as numbers; 'save ALL' makes a 'Variables' sheet (name/value) plus one sheet per list/table. CSV files start with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel shows emoji.
runner_semantics.live_frames: When the browser is headless (always in server mode): after every step and, throttled to every 0.5 s, during pauses and while waiting for elements, send {event:'frame', src: JPEG data URL (CDP Page.captureScreenshot quality 55), url, title}. Read url/title first; if an alert is open that raises and the frame is skipped.
runner_semantics.popups: unhandled_prompt_behavior='ignore' on every browser so frames/commands never auto-close an alert before a popup block handles it.
runner_semantics.stop: Stop flag checked before each block, in pauses and on every wait poll.

websocket_protocol.GET /ws/ping: Accepts (if Origin allowed) and sends {event:'pong', server: bool}, then closes.

GET /ws/run.origin_check: Origin header must match BLOCKBOTS_ORIGINS, else close code 1008. No Origin (non-browser clients) is allowed.

client_to_server.text: reply to an ask event (max 2000 chars)

server_to_client.path: absolute path on the runner computer

server_to_client.question: text (editor shows a prompt and replies with action 'answer')

server_to_client.text: 'All N steps passed!' or the failure reason

GET /ws/run.concurrency: asyncio.Semaphore(BLOCKBOTS_MAX_RUNS) in server mode; the slot is held until 'done' (browser really closed). Client disconnect stops the run.

http_endpoints.GET /: Editor (static/index.html; static files mounted at / last so routes win)
http_endpoints.GET /playground, /playground/frame: Practice site; other files in static/playground are served by the static mount
http_endpoints.GET /api/tests, GET|PUT|DELETE /api/test: Local mode only: saved tests in tests/<name>.json (name sanitized to [\w\- ], max 60)
http_endpoints.GET /shots/*, /scraped/*: Local mode only: screenshots and saved files

server_mode_security: Run the container on its own Docker network shared only with the reverse proxy (cannot reach databases or other services)

Address guard for go to / new tab / downloads: only http/https; hostname resolved and every address must be ip.is_global; exception: localhost/127.0.0.1 on the runner's own port with path starting /playground
upload_file refused; nothing written to disk (outputs are downloads, screenshots are data URLs, saved-tests API disabled)
Non-root user in the image; Chromium flags --headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-dev-shm-usage --disable-gpu --window-size=1280,800

Limits: BLOCKBOTS_MAX_RUNS simultaneous runs, BLOCKBOTS_MAX_SECONDS per run ('The test ran longer than 5 minutes, so I stopped it.'), waits capped at 60 s, downloads capped at 15 MB, step delay capped at 2 s

playground.purpose: Practice website served by the runner at /playground. Every block's default field value targets something here, so blocks work the moment they are dropped in.

elements.#name, #hello-btn, #greeting: Type a name; button (or Enter) shows 'Hello, <name>! 👋'
elements.#pet, #pizza, #pet-msg: Select Cat/Dog/Dragon (values cat/dog/dragon) and checkbox; message updates
elements.#reveal-btn, #loading, #secret: Shows ⏳ Loading… then '🎉 You found the secret!' after 2 s
elements.#double-box, #right-box, #hover-box: Change text on double-click / right-click / hover
elements.#alert-btn, #confirm-btn, #prompt-btn, #: alert('Hello from the playground!'), confirm('Do you like robots?'), prompt('What is your robot called?')
elements.#star, #basket: Drag the star into the basket with plain mouse events (not HTML5 DnD, so Selenium can do it) -> 'Caught the star! ⭐'

elements.#shop .product (.name .price a.more): 4 toys: Rocket Kit $12.99, Robot Dog $24.50, Magic Cube $7.25, Dino Lamp $18.00

Dockerfile: apt-get install --no-install-recommends chromium chromium-driver fonts-dejavu-core fonts-noto-color-emoji

standalone_docker_compose.note: Standalone, the runner serves the editor itself at / and detects server mode via /ws/ping. Put it behind HTTPS (e.g. nginx/Caddy) and set BLOCKBOTS_ORIGINS to your site.

behind_an_existing_site.editor: Copy static/ (minus playground/) into the site's public folder (e.g. /blockly-selenium/) and embed /blockly-selenium/index.html?runner=/blockly-runner in an iframe
behind_an_existing_site.nginx: location /blockly-runner/ { resolver 127.0.0.11 valid=30s ipv6=off; set $r http://blockly_runner:8000; rewrite ^/blockly-runner/(.*)$ /$1 break; proxy_pass $r; proxy_http_version 1.1; proxy_set_header Upgrade $http_upgrade; proxy_set_header Connection "upgrade"; proxy_set_header Host $host; proxy_read_timeout 600s; proxy_send_timeout 600s; }
behind_an_existing_site.caching: Serve the copied editor files with Cache-Control: no-cache (they are not fingerprinted)
behind_an_existing_site.network: Runner on its own Docker network shared only with nginx

acceptance_tests: Every block type in static/js/blocks.js has a matching @block function in runner.py and vice versa
All three examples pass end to end against the playground in local mode and in server mode

Make a variable 'number_of_vacancies', set the scrape #vacancies block to it, drag its chip into say -> block shows 'say ⟨number_of_vacancies⟩'; Run -> diary shows '3' and the Variables box shows number_of_vacancies 3
Failing check shows red ✗, shake and a reason bubble; Stop marks the current block stopped; missing element waits then explains

Server mode: go to 127.0.0.1 / 192.168.x / 10.x / localhost:5432 / file:// are refused with friendly messages; upload_file refused; /api/tests returns 404; a third run waits when MAX_RUNS=2; long runs stop at MAX_SECONDS
Server mode outputs arrive as 'download' events (Excel/CSV/JSON/PNG/PDF/HTML); local mode writes them to scraped/
Popup blocks still work with live frames on (alert not auto-dismissed)
Live browser window updates during waits and shows the current URL; ⤢ enlarges it
Hosted editor (?runner=...) through a path-prefix reverse proxy connects to wss://<host>/<prefix>/ws/run
No console errors in the editor
